criteria.note: The corpus (schema warp.intent_corpus/v1, .warp/intent_corpus.py) is built FROM the project's OWN record and reuses recorded data only (NG5). I built it fresh via open_corpus, which loads validate.py and decision.py BY PATH and injects the repo's own readers (parse_yamlish for specs and plans, json for proofs and verdicts, proof_digest for a proof's identity, plan_registry for plans, load_repo_contract for the contract, decision.load_record for decisions); no reader is reimplemented and there is no second parser. Over this repository it indexed 120 specs (with acceptance criteria), 116 proofs (criteria statuses, checks, bound commit, proof digest), 117 verdicts, 15 plans, 463 events, and the architecture contract (contract_present true); decisions stand down to 0 (no .warp/decisions/ here). FAIL-CLOSED-AT-BUILD reproduced independently over temp trees: a spec with no front matter, a spec front matter with a tab (outside the parser subset), and a proof manifest that is not valid JSON each raise IntentCorpusError by name. ADOPTION-SAFE reproduced: an empty tree builds .empty True and every query stands down (ungoverned Trace or empty change list, no error). PROBE6 confirmed the source contains NO write op (no write_text/write_bytes/mkdir/json.dump/open-for-write) - it is a pure read over the record, so it builds no store and adds no instrumentation.

The runtime query interface is a READ over the record, reproduced independently against the module loaded from disk. trace(WARP-1202) returns the governance chain: its real acceptance criteria (what it PROMISED), the proof that PROVED it (proof digest starting sha256:, per-criterion statuses, checks, bound commit), the VERDICT that reviewed it, and citations that resolve to the REAL proof/WARP-1202/manifest.json and proof/WARP-1202/verdict.json. governing_spec resolves a behavior by recorded spec id (WARP-1202, matched_by spec_id) AND by declared footprint match (.warp/evidence.py -> WARP-1202, matched_by footprint, in candidates). proof_for_commit(96fb65f...) maps a real commit to its proof and verdict. recent_changes reads BOTH sources: I exercised the REAL default_git_reader (an actual synchronous git log, not the injected fake) over .warp/intent_corpus.py and it returned the real 0a826eb commit and joined 2 events from events.jsonl whose commit matches; it also stands down to [] on a non-git dir. trace_incident assembles the artifact-grounded trace for a seeded incident (governing spec + criteria + proof + verdict + recent changes over the footprint). This is the READ W4 diagnoses FROM; the module composes no prose diagnosis and emits no proposal.

THE NO-FABRICATION PROPERTY IS REAL (the crux) - reproduced independently, not by re-reading the builder's tests. (a) An ungoverned behavior returns Trace(governed=False) whose reason names 'no governing artifact' and which carries NOTHING invented: spec_id None, criteria [], proof None, verdicts [], citations []. trace() of an unknown spec id is likewise ungoverned and invents nothing. A random English sentence resolves to ungoverned (PROBE2), and there is NO over-broad footprint glob (like '*') in any real spec that could over-match arbitrary behavior (PROBE1). (b) A spec with no recorded proof traces with proof None (honest absence), never a fabricated proof. (c) THE LOAD-BEARING TOOTH: I subclassed IntentCorpus so governing_spec fabricates a governor (returns an arbitrary spec) for an ungoverned behavior - the no-fabrication check went RED (governed became True); the real corpus stays GREEN; the on-disk module is byte-unchanged. (d) THE PROOF-GROUNDING TOOTH: I subclassed so trace fills an absent proof with a fabricated one - the proof-grounding check went RED (proof became not None); the real trace reports None. FAIL-CLOSED by name on a malformed query reproduced: trace(''), trace(None), trace('   '), governing_spec(''), recent_changes(None), proof_for_commit(''), area_of(None), area_of(123), an incident naming neither affected_spec nor affected_behavior, and an incident that is not a dict each raise IntentCorpusError. The corpus can NOT invent a governing spec, proof, or verdict for an ungoverned behavior; diagnosis-from-artifacts holds.

findings.text: FULL W3 SCOPE DELIVERED WITH NO DODGE AND THE NO-FABRICATION PROPERTY IS REAL (the crux). Every mandated behavior is present and grounded: behavior -> governing spec, change -> proof + verdict, recent changes from git AND events, module -> contract area with an honest C7 stand-down, all as a cited read over the record that reuses the injected validate/decision readers and adds no store, parser, event, or write op (NG5). The load-bearing guarantee holds and is NON-VACUOUS: an ungoverned behavior returns a truthful 'no governing artifact' with nothing invented, an absent proof reports None, and BOTH teeth go RED under mutation (fabricated governor; fabricated dropped proof) - I reproduced each independently against the on-disk module and confirmed the module is byte-unchanged after. Unlike prior W-items caught dropping mandated behavior, nothing here is dropped, substituted, or made toothless.

proof_for_commit MATCHES BY BIDIRECTIONAL PREFIX, so a degenerate short commit query is over-broad (non-blocking). _require_query rejects only empty/non-string commits, not short ones, and the match is pc.startswith(commit) OR commit.startswith(pc); a 1-character query like '0' returned 10 proofs. This is imprecise on degenerate input but NOT a no-fabrication violation - every returned entry is a REAL proof file bound to a REAL recorded commit (I confirmed all 10 hits resolve to existing files), nothing is invented, and a real responder passes full 40-char shas (the bidirectional match exists precisely to bridge a short git sha against a full recorded sha). Recommendation for the W4 responder loop: query with the full sha, or add a minimum-length guard, so an over-broad prefix cannot dilute a diagnosis with unrelated-but-real proofs.

THE DECISION-RECORD INDEX STANDS DOWN TO ZERO IN THIS REPO, so its populated path rests on the adoption-safe posture rather than a real fixture (non-blocking). AC1 lists recorded decisions as one indexed artifact type, and _read_decisions is wired through the injected decision.load_record, but this repository has no .warp/decisions/*.yaml (PLAN-0012's D1-D5 live in the plan front matter, not the decision store), so stats.decisions is 0 and decision(id) returns None for every id here. The reader degrades honestly (adoption safe: absent dir or absent loader -> {}), and the selftest does not seed a populated decisions dir either, so the decision() query is exercised only over the empty case. This matches how the corpus treats every absent artifact class and is honest, but the populated decision-index path is unproven over a real decision record. Recommendation: seed a decisions fixture in the W4/W11 conformance so decision() is proven over a real warp.decision/v1 record end to end.

HONEST DEFERRALS AND GENERATED-FILE HANDLING ARE CORRECT. The run_all wiring and init lay-down are deferred to WARP-1211 (W11), matching how W1 and W2 shipped their organs unwired; because validate.py is not edited it stays at 925 lines under the module_lines budget. The capabilities entry, the spec, and the module docstrings honestly name W4 (the first consumer, this module being the query surface it reads and NOT the agent), W2/W5/W6/W7, and W11 as later separate acts, and state the module emits no diagnosis or proposal - nothing is implied built that is not. specs/index.md is changed in the commit but is a GENERATED artifact (regenerated by update_index.py, check_generated clean, no drift), consistent with the W1/W2 commits.
